evidence.source: 李学勤主编，《字源》，天津古籍出版社、辽宁人民出版社，2012；direct inspection of supplied original scan attachment 1 and exact paragraph crops attachments 2–3; PDF p. 71, printed p. 59; attachment SHA-256 values as supplied bind the inspected image files.
evidence.field: Lower-left headword 茶 entry: printed reading, formation, original meaning, and same-page continuation
evidence.text: The lower-left headword visibly reads 茶, without the extra horizontal stroke that distinguishes 荼. The entry gives the reading tú and says it is a phono-semantic character formed from 艸 with 余 as phonetic; it identifies 苦菜 as the original meaning. The prose continues at the top right of the same printed page 59: it compares the extension to bitter/painful senses, cites 《书·汤诰》, and quotes 孔颖达 citing 《释草》 that 茶 is 苦菜, concluding that its bitter taste was borrowed metaphorically for human suffering. This entry's proposed original meaning and analogy do not establish that 苦菜 was the source of the later tea sense. The crop's claim is scoped to headword 茶 and must not be confused with nearby entries 薔 or 蘩.

evidence.source: 《说文解字》 text as presented by 汉语多功能字库, entry 茶 / 荼; consulted online.
evidence.field: Traditional graph analysis, sound component and proposed original referent
evidence.text: This dictionary account states that 茶 is a later graph, originally written 荼, analyzed as 艸 semantic plus 余 phonetic, and gives tea plant as the original referent. This differs from the 字源 page 59 entry's 苦菜 claim; preserve them as attributed, differing accounts rather than merging them.

evidence.field: Graph history: proposed derivation of 茶 from 荼 and chronology of differentiated forms
evidence.text: The accessible article text attributes to 王观国 a systematic discussion of 茶/荼 development and reports a proposal that 茶 was formed by omitting a stroke from 荼. The article itself offers a chronology for popularization and reports inconsistency between some artifact spellings and lexicographic accounts; as the page timed out when opened directly, treat this only as a lead and do not rely on its detailed interpretation as directly inspected source content.
